title: Admission simulator scenarios and ops checklist
content:
Purpose:
This note is a working sketch for an admission-control simulator harness and the accompanying ops checklist that platform teams can use to validate routing and admission strategies before rolling them into production. Goal: reason about combined effects of token banks, queue-depth admission, and GPU utilization hysteresis across multi-region routing with spillover.

Design principles (short):
- Keep simulator conservative: prefer false positives (predict drop) over false negatives.
- Model the whole control loop: ingress -> admission decision -> router -> GPU execution queue -> completion -> telemetry feedback.
- Capture time scales: 100ms (fast admit), 10s (autoscale), 5m (billing/aggregation).
- Allow per-tenant variability and warm KV-cache effects.

Key concepts we want to exercise:
- Token-fence (per-tenant credit fences that isolate short bursts) vs global token-bucket.
- Queue-depth admission with hysteresis windows: low/high watermarks, delay before re-open.
- GPU occupancy signal fusion: immediate GPU SM% + short rolling average + predicted headroom from scheduled batches.
- Multi-region spill routing: cost/latency penalty functions when spilling traffic to another region.
- Stochastic deferred-admit: probabilistic admit rate when near capacity to avoid synchronized retries.

Simulator components (event-driven):
- Arrival generator: poisson, burst (peak = x*baseline), pareto+bursty tails.
- Per-request attributes: tenant_id, model, seq_len, streaming=yes/no, kv_hit_rate.
- Admission policies: token-fence, token-bucket, queue-threshold, gpu-utilization-threshold, composite-rule (AND/OR/priority lanes).
- Router: policy + cost model + route preference (region local -> dedicated -> fallback-hosted).
- Backend model: execution time = base_latency(model, seq_len) * (1 + contention_factor), gpu queue model (service times, preemption).
- Telemetry producer: emits sample windows (100ms, 1s, 10s) for queue_depth, token_balance, gpu_util, tail_latencies.

Suggested simulation scenarios (priority order):
1) Short flash burst (fast spike): 20x baseline RPS for 10s, then back to baseline. Test: token-fence holds tenant; spill to regional pool; measure p95 latency, rejected rate.
2) Sustained medium spike: 3x baseline for 30m. Test: autoscale triggers, check that admission reduces cost by shedding low-priority lanes rather than harming SLO for high-priority lanes.
3) Regional outage + reroute: remove 50% capacity in region-A mid-run, observe reroute latency penalty and token-bucket backpressure across regions.
4) High-variance tail workload: Pareto inter-arrival with alpha=1.2, heavy sequence-length variance. Test queue-slopes and deferred-admit effectiveness.
5) Coordinated retries storm: clients retry exponentially but share similar backoff time. Test stochastic deferred-admit to avoid synchronized spikes.
6) Cache-warmth delta: same request surface but differing KV cache hit rates (10% vs 90%), check that routing favors cache-warm hosts for cost and latency.

Metrics to capture (always capture raw + windowed):
- admitted_count, rejected_count, deferred_count
- queue_depth (per-backend) sampled at 100ms
- gpu_util_percent (instant) and gpu_util_rolling_10s
- per-tenant token_balance and drain_rate
- request_latency (p50/p95/p99) end-to-end and backend-only
- tail queuing time (time waiting before execution)
- cost_estimate (tokens consumed * unit_cost + cross-region-penalty)
- retry_attempts and cluster-level rps after retry windows

Config matrix (example knobs to sweep):
- token_bucket_capacity: [50, 200, 1000] tokens
- token_replenish_rate: [5/s, 20/s, 100/s]
- queue_high_watermark: [50, 150, 500] requests
- queue_low_watermark: [20, 60, 200] requests
- gpu_util_threshold_warn: [65%, 80%]
- gpu_util_threshold_block: [85%, 95%]
- deferred_admit_prob: [0.1, 0.33, 0.5] when in soft-block state
- spill_penalty_ms: [20, 60, 150] (added latency when spilling region)

Example policy combinations to validate:
- Conservative: token-fence(tenant) AND queue-depth-block AND gpu-block -> maximizes isolation, more rejects, lower tail-latency for accepted requests.
- Opportunistic: global-token-bucket OR (queue-depth < high) -> more accepted requests, higher tail-latency under stress.
- Priority lanes: lane0(high) bypass token_fence up to reserved_tokens, lane1(low) uses token-fence -> ensures business-critical customers keep capacity.

Runbook / ops checklist for rolling a new admission policy (draft):
Pre-flight (local & staging):
- [ ] Run simulator full-sweep against target policy with both synthetic and historical traffic replay (use 7 days of anonymized trace).
- [ ] Confirm p99 degradation < 15% compared to baseline for top 10 tenants.
- [ ] Verify rejected_rate per-tenant matches SLAs (document expected thresholds).
- [ ] Smoke-test multi-region spill logic with fake region latency injection (50ms/100ms).
- [ ] Validate telemetry emission: queue_depth 100ms, token_balance 1s, gpu_util 100ms.
Canary rollout (prod small %):
- [ ] Enable policy for 5% of traffic (by tenant or route). Monitor 5m windows for: sudden increase in retries, cross-region egress, cost delta.
- [ ] If retry storms detected, immediately flip on synchronous backoff feature and reduce canary to 1%.
- [ ] Maintain human-on-call watch for first 30 minutes after change.
Scale-up (gradual):
- [ ] 5 -> 20 -> 50 -> 100% with 30m observation windows. Escalate and rollback on violations.
Rollback triggers (examples):
- p99 latency increases > 30% for any high-priority tenant for two consecutive windows.
- cross-region egress > budgeted % for the org.
- rejected_rate spikes > 3x expected for >15 minutes without server-side autoscale making progress.
Postmortem checks (after incidents):
- [ ] Correlate token_balance drops with tenant-level retries and client-side backoff patterns.
- [ ] Re-run simulator with exact trace and confirm whether policy would have prevented the failure.
- [ ] Update thresholds if simulator shows systematic over/under-sensitivity.

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- How do we weight GPU-preemptibility of short streaming requests vs long synchronous batches when computing predicted headroom?
- Should token fences be hierarchical (org -> team -> tenant) and how to bound cross-tenant spill impact?
- Integration with scheduler: simulator assumes immediate scale-up; need to model scale latency + warmup cost (KV cache penalties).
- Need a standard format for replay traces that includes model, seq_len, kv_hit boolean, and synthetic client backoff behavior.

Practical next steps (this doc):
1) Build simple event-driven simulator prototype (Python) with pluggable arrival-generator and policy modules. Use existing anonymized traces to seed arrival distributions.
2) Create a canonical sweep of the config-matrix with automated report that outputs risk heatmap (latency vs rejected_rate vs cost).
3) Add an ops checklist github issue template and link to canary experiment dashboard.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally informal. Please add scenario suggestions, missing metrics, and concrete thresholds you want to validate in the simulator.
- If you own a tenant with tight SLOs, add your top-10 query patterns to the trace repo so we test realistic worst-case behaviour.

Quick simulation config snippet (YAML-like pseudo):
---
arrival: {type: burst, multiplier: 20, duration_s: 10}
policy: {token_fence: true, fence_capacity: 200, queue_high: 150, gpu_block_pct: 90, deferred_prob: 0.33}
regions: [{name: A, capacity: 100}, {name: B, capacity: 80, extra_latency_ms: 60}]
metrics_windows: [100ms, 1s, 10s]
---

End of draft.
